note: Promotion to the tracked schema (roadmap Phase 1 backfill). Track groups follow the (XX) prefixes already embedded in the source theme names; only empty fields are filled.

themes.description: Marking out and measuring before cutting — the discipline that decides whether parts fit.
Joining two pieces of wood so they stay joined — the basic joints and choosing between them.
Hacksaw, snips and files — cutting and finishing metal safely at the bench.
The stitches and seams that survive washing and wearing — sewing as construction, not decoration.
Mixing, forming and curing — the wet materials that become permanent, and the timing that governs them.
The working drawing — dimensions, views, materials list — good enough that someone else could build it.
Sanding, sealing, painting and edges — the last ten percent that makes a made thing look meant.
Building to a real person's need and measurements, checked with them before, during and after.
Reading a failure for its lesson — what broke, why, and the change the next version carries.
Materials, time and overhead totalled honestly — what the thing actually cost to make.
The questions and checks that find a fault before a screwdriver moves — symptom, history, most likely cause.

themes.theme: The four repairs every household needs (RP)
themes.description: The repeating household repairs — leaks, sticking, wobbles, blockages — mastered as standard procedures.
Buttons, hems, tears and zips — the clothing repairs that keep garments in service for years.
The small engine's usual failures — fuel, spark, air — diagnosed in order on a real machine.
The electronic repairs still open to a careful amateur — connections, batteries, switches — and the line where danger starts.
Loose joints, broken legs and worn surfaces — bringing real furniture back to use.
The bicycle as the repairable machine — punctures, brakes and gears serviced with basic tools.
Repair cafés and fix-it events — repairing in public so the skill and the habit spread.
Judging repair against replacement honestly — safety, parts, cost and the repair that throws good money after bad.
Walking somebody else through a repair with their hands on the tools, not yours.

tracks.name: Reuse and what things are worth

themes.theme: Where a thing goes when you throw it (RU)
themes.description: Following real waste from your bin to its end — landfill, export, recycling — and what actually happens there.
Metals, textiles, timber and plastic as materials with prices — reading value in what others discard.
Recognising designed-in failure — glued batteries, unavailable parts — and buying against it.
Disassembly as harvesting — recovering fasteners, timber, motors and parts without destroying them.
The plastic types, which are genuinely recycled where you live, and reducing the ones that are not.
Designing from the salvage pile — letting available materials shape what gets made.
Rescuing edible surplus safely — gleaning, sharing and preserving what would have been thrown.

themes.theme: Water and materials in a workshop (RU)
themes.description: Running a workshop lean — offcuts, solvents and water managed so little is wasted or dumped.
An object's whole life traced — materials, use, repairs, afterlife — and the choices that lengthen it.
Pricing, describing and selling used goods honestly — the second-hand transaction done well from both sides.

themes.theme: The tool that will hurt you (TL)
themes.description: Each tool's specific danger named before first use — and the habits that keep hands whole.
Restoring an edge — knives, chisels, blades — and why a sharp tool is the safer one.
A working bench arranged for real work — height, light, holding, and everything findable.
Tool libraries, lending and sharing — getting capability without owning everything.
Cleaning, oiling and storing tools so they outlive their owner.
The power tools' rules — guards, grip, workpiece held, cord managed — demonstrated before speed.
Squares, levels, gauges and calipers — reading them truly and checking them against themselves.
Shared workshop discipline — induction, booking, leaving the machine as found — so the space survives its users.
The slow injuries of a workshop — extraction, masks and ear protection actually used.
Building the helper that makes repetition accurate — the jig as stored precision.
Pricing labour and materials so the work pays — the quote, the day rate and the job that loses money.
The first paid job end to end — agreement, delivery, payment and the review that brings the second.
The numbers under a small workshop — costs, throughput, break-even — read from a real or modelled month.
The apprenticeship routes where you live — trades, entry, pay during training — mapped from real providers.
The tickets and certificates that measurably raise pay in a trade, and the cheapest path to each.
Being employed in a trade — the site rules, the expectations and the reputation that follows you.
Passing a trade on — breaking skills into teachable steps and supervising early work without doing it.
A local trade in decline studied honestly — why it is fading and what its skills still transfer to.
The new trades appearing locally — solar, e-bikes, retrofit — and the earliest route in.

themes.theme: A career that lasts thirty years (TR)
themes.description: A trade career mapped across decades — the body, the tools, the moves into teaching, inspecting or owning.
